metric_rationale: The design contains 8 unique pairs (trials 1-6, 13-14; 48 of the 96 trials) in which the option favored by the first discriminating cue in the validity cascade is exactly the option that LOSES the equal-weight tally. On these conflict trials the two theories make opposite directional predictions with no overlap: TTB chooses the cue-cascade winner with probability (1-eps)*sigmoid(beta)+eps/2 (expected ~0.84 across the parameter range, always >= 0.5), while Tallying chooses that same option with probability 1 - [(1-eps)*sigmoid(beta*margin)+eps/2] (expected ~0.16, always <= 0.5). The metric is the proportion of conflict trials on which the subject picked the TTB-favored (tally-losing) option. It is computed from the stimuli themselves, not from a model fit, and averages over 48 trials per subject, so per-subject binomial noise is tiny; the only across-subject spread comes from individual noise levels (beta, epsilon), which shifts both theories symmetrically toward 0.5 but can never make them cross it. The expected between-theory gap (~0.68) dwarfs the per-subject SD (~0.1), giving a very large Welch t at N=25. Crucially, the metric is not trivially true of TTB: any subject who weights cues equally, or who is swayed by the 3-4 vs 1 feature majority, drives it below 0.5.

The metric is the proportion of choices that go to the option favoured by the first (highest-validity) discriminating cue, restricted to exactly those trials where the tally does NOT back that option: the 2-2 tally ties (Family D, pairs 9-12) and the graded directional-conflict pairs (Family E, pairs 13-16). This isolates the only place the two heuristics make qualitatively different, non-overlapping commitments, and it deliberately excludes the Family-C margin ladder, whose contrast vanishes whenever beta is large (both models then predict the same flat near-ceiling accuracy), which would only dilute the signal and add noise.

Predicted values: under Take-The-Best every included trial has a discriminating top cue, so the model chooses that option with probability (1-eps)*sigmoid(beta)+eps/2 on ALL of them, giving a metric near 0.85-0.9 for typical parameters and only mildly modulated by the lapse rate. Under Tallying the same trials split into two blocks with predictions that are both far below that: the tally-tie trials force exactly 0.5 regardless of beta and epsilon, and the conflict trials force the OPPOSITE choice (probability eps/2, i.e. near 0.1), so the pooled value sits around 0.3. The expected between-theory gap is roughly 0.55 on a 0-1 scale.

Variance is kept tight because (a) 48 of the 96 trials qualify, so binomial noise per subject is small; (b) under Tallying the tie block is parameter-free (exactly chance for every subject) and the conflict block saturates near zero, so subject-to-subject spread is driven only by the lapse rate; (c) under TTB the value is a single sigmoid-plus-lapse number, again with limited spread. Crucially, the metric is not trivially true for Tallying: Tallying could in principle score anywhere from 0 to 1 here, and any systematic above-chance preference for the top-cue option on the 2-2 splits (which Tallying must call at exactly 50/50) pushes the metric toward the TTB value.

Both theories are pinned near the same level on the agreement families (D: full dominance, G: only the 93% expert speaks, H: only the 55% expert speaks) \u2014 in all of these the option carrying the 1(s) is favoured by TTB and by any positive-weight compensatory rule alike. The conflict families (A, B, E, F) are constructed so the true-validity cascade and the left-to-right positional weighting point to opposite options. The metric is the WITHIN-SUBJECT difference: (rate of choosing the TTB-implied option on agreement trials) minus (rate on conflict trials).

Under Take-The-Best the choice probability is sigmoid(beta) mixed with lapse on EVERY discriminating trial regardless of which cue does the discriminating, so both terms have the same expectation and the difference is ~0 for every subject regardless of beta and epsilon; the only spread is binomial sampling noise over 36 and 48 trials (var <= ~0.012). Under WADD-\u03b3 with positional misattribution the conflict trials are answered against the TTB option (weights: col0 \u2248 .44, col1 \u2248 .25 vs col3 \u2248 .10, col4 \u2248 .12 at \u03bb=.8, \u03b3=1.5), giving conflict TTB-consistency well below .5 while agreement consistency stays high; the difference is large and positive (~.2 at the weakest \u03b2, ~.8 at moderate \u03b2). Family C is deliberately excluded because the competitor is at chance there and would dilute the contrast. Because the metric self-normalises each subject against their own agreement-trial determinacy, it is insensitive to the wide beta/epsilon heterogeneity that would otherwise inflate between-subject variance for TTB.

The metric isolates the trials on which the two theories make OPPOSITE directional predictions with a large positional-WADD margin: families A (col0 .60 vs col3 .86), B (col0 vs col5 .78) and F (col3 vs the col0+col2 coalition). Take-The-Best follows the true validity cascade (col1 > col3 > col5 > col4 > col0 > col2) and therefore picks the option that positional WADD rejects on every one of these 30 trials; positional misattribution (weights re-sorted descending across display columns, giving col0 the largest subjective weight) picks the opposite option with |d| ~ .26-.39. The metric is simply the proportion of those conflict trials on which the subject chose the positionally-favoured option. Under TTB this is essentially the flip-noise floor ((1-eps)*sigmoid(-beta)+eps/2, roughly .05-.30), under the advocated model it is well above .5 (roughly .6-.95 depending on beta). Trials with |d| < .20 (families C, D, E) are excluded because the advocated model is near-indifferent there, which would only add between-subject noise; trials where both models agree (G, H, I) are excluded because they carry no directional contrast. This yields a large mean gap (~.5) while keeping each subject's value tightly bounded within its theory, since the sign of the prediction is invariant over both theories' whole parameter boxes.

Within-subject contrast designed to cancel every free noise parameter of Take-The-Best while maximally loading the competitor's strict-unanimity consensus premium.

Cell HIGH = pairs [1,1,1,1,1] vs [1,1,1,1,0] (and mirror): the two options differ on the LOWEST-validity cue only, and the winner's panel is unanimous. Cell LOW = pairs where one option carries a single weak endorsement (cue3 or cue5) and the other is the all-zero (also unanimous) panel; here the weakly endorsed option is the TTB winner but its panel is maximally incoherent while its rival is unanimous.

TTB: in both cells the first discriminating cue favours the target option, so the choice probability is exactly (1-eps)*sigmoid(beta)+eps/2 in BOTH cells, whatever beta and eps are. The contrast is therefore identically 0 in expectation for every subject, regardless of that subject's determinacy or lapse rate — the metric is immune to TTB's (very wide) parameter heterogeneity, leaving only small binomial sampling noise (12 + 24 trials per subject).

RVW-DE+/U: the weighted-evidence term is essentially the same tiny w5 (or w3) in both cells, but the direction-blind premium rho*|2m-1|^q with high q flips sign between cells: in HIGH the premium (~+rho) adds to the cue, in LOW it (~-rho) opposes the single endorsement, driving predicted accuracy from ~.94 down to ~.06-.13. Its predicted contrast is therefore large and positive (~.7-.9), with only moderate spread from rho/q/beta heterogeneity.

So: TTB predicts ~0, the competitor predicts a large positive step, and neither prediction is trivially guaranteed by the metric's construction (both cells are ordinary accuracy proportions on distinct trial types).

Every term is a WITHIN-subject contrast between two cells in which Take-The-Best makes the *same* one-reason decision at the *same* flat probability sigmoid(beta)(1-eps)+eps/2, so each contrast has expectation exactly 0 under TTB regardless of that subject's beta and lapse rate (only binomial noise remains, ~8 trials/cell). (i) L1-L4: TTB stops at the .93 cue in both, picking the col2 option identically whether the rival carries one weak endorsement or four; RVW's flattened weights let the growing coalition overturn the top cue, so the col2 option falls from ~.55 to ~.03. (ii) U4-U1: both cells differ on col3 ALONE, so TTB's discriminating cue and its winner are identical; RVW's strict-unanimity premium makes the all-zero panel beat a lone weak endorsement (~.15) while a 5/5 panel beats a 4/5 panel (~.97). (iii) V2-V1: same manipulation at col0, again a single flat TTB level but a ~.22 vs ~.98 split under RVW. Averaging the three contrasts cuts per-subject binomial noise while preserving a mean gap of roughly 0.7 (RVW) versus 0.0 (TTB); because the TTB side is pinned at zero with only sampling variance, and the RVW side is driven by shared, strongly-signed effects, the between-subject spread stays small relative to the gap.
